editions.signal: Today’s strongest signal is that AI engineering is splitting into two simultaneous races: make capable models cheaper and more deployable, while making agent execution more constrained, inspectable, and reliable. Open weights, specialized cyber access, massive inference financing, typed agent actions, and deliberate multi-model review all point toward a more modular AI stack.

Today’s strongest signal is that frontier AI is becoming a systems discipline: model capability is still climbing quickly, but operational advantage is shifting toward controlled agent runtimes, cheaper open-weight inference, better serving topology, and mechanisms that let agents learn from previous work without becoming ungovernable.

Today’s strongest signal is that AI engineering is moving beyond model selection into full-stack operational design: concurrent coding agents, inference-stack optimization, agent provenance, and tighter consolidation of browser/tool surfaces are becoming first-class engineering concerns.

The most important theme is the transition from models that answer to agents that operate — and the engineering controls needed once those agents can modify repositories, use tools, spend money, and probe real systems.
